title: STATE POLICE RELEASE ACCIDENT DETAILS
full_story:
State Police have released more preliminary information on a three-vehicle crash that killed 25-year-old Madison Burton of Odin Thursday night on I 57.

The report indicates that Burton was parked on the shoulder of the interstate with her emergency flashers activated due to a flat tire.  A semi approaching activated its turn signal to indicate a lane change to the passing lane to obey state law.  But the semi driver then observed a pickup truck rapidly approaching and changing lanes causing him to cease the lane change to prevent a collision with the pickup.  Then the pickup swiftly returned to the driving lane in an attempt to pass the semi and went onto the shoulder to continue passing the semi.  State Police say during the maneuver, the pickup collided with Burton’s disabled car parked on the shoulder.  The impact caused Burton’s car to overturn into the ditch.  The pickup driver then re-entered the roadway, struck the semi, and then ran into the ditch.

Burton was transferred to Good Samaritan Hospital where she was pronounced dead in the emergency room.  The driver of the pickup, who has not been identified, was also taken to a hospital for treatment of injuries.

title: CROP PROGRESS AND CONDITION
full_story:
In its latest crop progress and condition report released yesterday, the USDA reported 14% of Illinois corn had dented, compared to 16% the same week last year and the five-year average of 10%.  Soybeans blooming reached 77%, slightly ahead of last year and the average pace.

The USDA reported Monday that there were 5.7 days suitable for fieldwork in the week ending August 9th.  Statewide, the average temperature was 74.8 degrees, .2 degrees above normal.  Precipitation averaged .42 inches, 0.37 inches below normal.  Topsoil moisture supply was rated 4% very short, 20% short, 70% adequate, and 6% surplus.  Subsoil moisture supply was rated 5% very short, 23% short, 65% adequate, and 7% surplus.

Corn silking reached 96%, compared to the 5-year average of 97%.  Corn dough reached 64%, equal to the 5-year average.  Corn dented reached 14%, compared to the 5-year average of 10%.  Corn condition was rated 3% very poor, 8% poor, 28% fair, 48% good, and 13% excellent.

Soybeans blooming reached 92%, compared to the 5-year average of 93%.  Soybeans setting pods reached 77%, compared to the 5-year average of 74%.  Soybeans condition was rated 3% very poor, 7% poor, 31% fair, 47% good, and 12% excellent.

title: ISP NITE PATROLS
full_story:
Illinois State Police (ISP) Troop 9 Commander, Lieutenant Bruce Waggoner, announces the ISP will conduct Nighttime Enforcement (NITE) patrols in Clay, Fayette, Wayne, Effingham, Marion, White, and Hamilton counties during August and September.  NITE patrols allow the ISP to focus on preventing, detecting, and taking enforcement action in response to impaired driving and occupant restraint violations especially between the hours of 9:00 pm and 6:00 am.

The number of unrestrained drivers killed in traffic crashes is significantly higher at nighttime and combined with impaired driving means even more traffic deaths during these critical hours.

Officers working the enforcement patrols will be watchful for motorists who show signs of impaired driving, improper seatbelt and child restraint usage, speeding, distracted driving, and other Illinois Vehicle Code violations.

Alcohol and drug impairment are estimated to be a factor in more than 47% of all fatal motor vehicle crashes in Illinois.  Over half of all fatal crashes in Illinois occur at night.  The NITE program allows officers to work even harder at removing dangerous impaired drivers from the road and making sure everyone is buckled up.  This project is funded through the Illinois Department of Transportation.

title: PLACARD PILOT PROGRAM
full_story:
Illinois Secretary of State Alexi Giannoulias launched a pilot program to make disability parking placards easier to obtain as a newly signed law expands accessible parking relief for families caring for children and individuals with disabilities.  The law allows the Secretary of State’s office to issue meter-exempt disability parking placards to legal guardians who transport individuals with disabilities who are incapable of driving.

To support the new law and improve customer service, the Secretary of State’s office is expanding in-person disability parking placard services to 14 additional Driver Services facilities across Illinois.  The new walk-in option allows customers to apply for or renew permanent and meter-exempt disability parking placards, reducing processing times for applications that were previously handled exclusively by mail through the Springfield office.

“Families caring for children and individuals with disabilities already face enough challenges; accessing parking while transporting a loved one to medical appointments, therapy, school or other essential services should not be an added burden,” Giannoulias said.  “This legislation provides meaningful relief for caregivers while making it easier for eligible Illinoisans to obtain the parking placards they need.  It’s another step toward delivering more accessible, customer-focused services across our state.”

Governor JB Pritzker signed House Bill 4843 into law on July 31st.  The measure took effect immediately.

Previously, meter-exempt parking benefits were available primarily for individuals with disabilities who drive themselves.  The new law addresses a longstanding gap by extending eligibility to caregivers who regularly transport individuals with significant disabilities.

The pilot program builds on the existing in-person disability parking placard service offered at the Springfield Flagship.  Participating Driver Services facilities include the Chicago Flagship, Chicago North, Chicago South, Chicago West, LaSalle, Robinson, Rockford, Champaign, Carbondale, Peoria, Quincy, Moline, Macomb and Granite City.

Meter-exempt parking placards allow eligible individuals to park in spaces reserved for persons with disabilities, such as at malls, grocery stores or retail locations.  They also exempt the holder from parking meter fees and time limitations, except where parking is limited to 30 minutes or less.

The provision expanding access to disability parking placards is part of a broader legislative package advanced by Giannoulias to modernize the Illinois Vehicle Code, improve accessibility and strengthen services for Illinois residents.

title: NEW AT THE IL STATE FAIR
full_story:
This year’s Illinois State Fair is ready to welcome you with unforgettable entertainment, incredible food, exciting attractions, and all the traditions you love.  Celebrating the theme, Miles of Smiles, every corner of the fairgrounds offers something new, sure to put a smile on your face.  Get a sneak peek at the brand-new experiences that await when the gates open.

Hungry for something new? This year’s food lineup features sweet, savory and everything in between from more than 120 food vendors.  Don’t miss the Golden Abe’s Fantastic Fair Food contest on Friday, to see who walks away with the coveted culinary bragging rights.

The first ever Illinois Best Bagger, sponsored by HyVee, will be held at 10 am on Monday, August 17th at the Grand Central Stage, testing the skills of grocery baggers as they compete for a potential $10,000 prize and a chance to compete at the national level in Las Vegas.

Dino Encounters features free animatronic rides, gyroscopes, a dinosaur museum, dinosaur digs, daily stage shows, puzzles and more in Happy Hollow.

Introducing the all-new Surfside Social Club – your go-to spot to soak in the best of the Fair along Route 66.  By day, it’s a laid-back social hub to enjoy a cold drink and live entertainment with family and friends.  As the sun sets, the energy turns up, neon lights glow, live music hits, and the Beer Garden comes alive.  Be sure to check out the Great American Sing-Along every day at 1 pm and 3 pm.
